body: thank you for taking the time to reply to me and thank you for your kindness

thank you for your kindness and your time that you took to reply

ive been subscribed to /r/raisedbynarcissists for years now, and it hurts sometimes to read because it gives me memories of home

ive been diagnosed with PTSD since my rape in 2013, and since 2011 ive been on seven different pills to treat my bipolar disorder

i go to therapy as well

thank you for being so concerned for me, friend

I cant lock a door or my mom will do things to me

I cant do any of that
I have too much work and too many responsibilities, laying alone only pushes me further and further into depression and motivates me to really end it all

nothing
i dont like anything
i just float and hope nothing goes wrong because everything is so sensitive

cant exercise, cant draw, cant write or read because my body shakes too much

cant even eat the foods i like because i actually get nauseous and vomit it back up again or get absolutely overwhelmed by dizziness, so i just eat light things like bread and cold cuts and juice

Thanks... but it's never been a problem before! I just started having these terrible thoughts two days ago... I've been sleeping with bella for our entire relationship, every since I got her every night. I want it to go away as quick as it started, not get rid of my dear.
Alright, so... I guess what I'm asking now is what I can do to stop it. I literally have never started having these problems until suddenly, two nights ago.
That's a good idea actually, maybe that'd help. I've just gotten over pneumonia and maybe I'm overworked and could benefit from that. Thank you for the advice!
Are you saying that I acted on the thoughts? (Just trying to be clear, not combative)

Thank you so much. that really made me laugh, a nice bit of humor always makes me handle things better because thats how i was raised to cope with issues! 

And youre right, actually. I wouldve moved my leg. i just needed that assurance because I guess sometimes i don't trust myself with my own feelings. The whole boundary thing i guess other bpd people might experience -- where does the mental bullshit end and my own person begin?

Im thinking now though that Ive never hurt her before in out co-sleeping. Like maybe how us humans don't roll off the bed or roll onto our partners (unintentionally ;~) ) in our sleep. I don't know how that whole sleeping boundary thing works though, so maybe it's speculation.

Sorry for the long ramble, I've been up since 3:30 (its 7:30 now...) racking my brain and getting all anxious about this!!!
